description.title: Microbe sample from Xylella fastidiosa subsp. fastidiosa CFBP8082
description.comment: Xylella fastidiosa is a bacterial plant pathogen disseminated across the Americas, while its presence is currently described in several European countries. Seven strains, available at the CIRM-CFBP (http://www.angers-nantes.inra.fr/cfbp/) were selected. Six strains were isolated in the USA from Vitis rotundifolia (CFBP7969), Vitis vinifera (CFBP 7970), Vitis SP (CFBP8341), Prunus dulcis (CFBP 8071) and Ambrosia artemifolia (CFBP 8082) and belong to X. fastidiosa subsp. fastidiosa. One strain was isolated in the USA from Vinca sp. (CFBP 8078) and belongs to X. fastidiosa subsp. multiplex. One strain was isolated from a coffee plant imported from the Costa Rica and intercepted in France (CFBP 8356) and belongs to X. fastidiosa subsp. sandyi. The taxonomic assignation to a subpecies was based on multiprimer PCR (Hernandez-Martinez et al., 2006), MLST scheme using 7 housekeeping genes (Yuan et al., 2010) and whole-genome sequencing unsing the Illumina Mi-Seq technology.

bioprojects.title: Xylella fastidiosa subsp. multiplex strain:CFBP 8417 Genome sequencing and assembly

description.title: Microbe sample from Xylella fastidiosa subsp. multiplex
description.comment: Xylella fastidiosa, a bacterial plant pathogen confined in the past to the Americas, recently emerged in Europe. It was first reported in natural settings in France from Polygala myrtifolia shrubs in Corsica in July 2015 and in south-eastern mainland France in October 2015. These ornamentals were symptomatic and presented severe leaf scorches. All contaminated samples from France presented bacteria belonging to X. fastidiosa subsp. multiplex, based on multiprimer PCR (Hernandez-Martinez et al., Phytopathol. 2006) analyses run on DNAs extracted from the infected plant samples. A MLST scheme was used to type these bacteria which are characterized by two X. fastidiosa subsp. multiplex bona fide sequence types, ST6 and ST7. Three strains were isolated from Polygala myrtifolia (CFBP 8416; ST7) and Spartium junceum (CFBP 8417 and CFBP 8418; ST6). The genomes of these strains were sequenced using the Illumina Mi-Seq technology.

description.title: Microbe sample from Xylella fastidiosa subsp. fastidiosa CFBP7970
description.comment: Xylella fastidiosa is a bacterial plant pathogen disseminated across the Americas, while its presence is currently described in several European countries. Seven strains, available at the CIRM-CFBP (http://www.angers-nantes.inra.fr/cfbp/) were selected. Six strains were isolated in the USA from Vitis rotundifolia (CFBP7969), Vitis vinifera (CFBP 7970), Vitis SP (CFBP8341), Prunus dulcis (CFBP 8071) and Ambrosia artemifolia (CFBP 8082) and belong to X. fastidiosa subsp. fastidiosa. One strain was isolated in the USA from Vinca sp. (CFBP 8078) and belongs to X. fastidiosa subsp. multiplex. One strain was isolated from a coffee plant imported from the Costa Rica and intercepted in France (CFBP 8356) and belongs to X. fastidiosa subsp. sandyi. The taxonomic assignation to a subpecies was based on multiprimer PCR (Hernandez-Martinez et al., 2006), MLST scheme using 7 housekeeping genes (Yuan et al., 2010) and whole-genome sequencing unsing the Illumina Mi-Seq technology.

description.title: Microbe sample from Xylella fastidiosa subsp. fastidiosa CFBP7969
description.comment: Xylella fastidiosa is a bacterial plant pathogen disseminated across the Americas, while its presence is currently described in several European countries. Seven strains, available at the CIRM-CFBP (http://www.angers-nantes.inra.fr/cfbp/) were selected. Six strains were isolated in the USA from Vitis rotundifolia (CFBP7969), Vitis vinifera (CFBP 7970), Vitis SP (CFBP8341), Prunus dulcis (CFBP 8071) and Ambrosia artemifolia (CFBP 8082) and belong to X. fastidiosa subsp. fastidiosa. One strain was isolated in the USA from Vinca sp. (CFBP 8078) and belongs to X. fastidiosa subsp. multiplex. One strain was isolated from a coffee plant imported from the Costa Rica and intercepted in France (CFBP 8356) and belongs to X. fastidiosa subsp. sandyi. The taxonomic assignation to a subpecies was based on multiprimer PCR (Hernandez-Martinez et al., 2006), MLST scheme using 7 housekeeping genes (Yuan et al., 2010) and whole-genome sequencing unsing the Illumina Mi-Seq technology.

bioprojects.title: Xylella fastidiosa subsp. multiplex strain:CFBP8416 Genome sequencing

description.title: Microbe sample from Xylella fastidiosa subsp. multiplex
description.comment: Xylella fastidiosa, a bacterial plant pathogen confined in the past to the Americas, recently emerged in Europe. It was first reported in natural settings in France from Polygala myrtifolia shrubs in Corsica in July 2015 and in south-eastern mainland France in October 2015. These ornamentals were symptomatic and presented severe leaf scorches. All contaminated samples from France presented bacteria belonging to X. fastidiosa subsp. multiplex, based on multiprimer PCR (Hernandez-Martinez et al., Phytopathol. 2006) analyses run on DNAs extracted from the infected plant samples. A MLST scheme was used to type these bacteria which are characterized by two X. fastidiosa subsp. multiplex bona fide sequence types, ST6 and ST7. Three strains were isolated from Polygala myrtifolia (CFBP 8416; ST7) and Spartium junceum (CFBP 8417 and CFBP 8418; ST6). The genomes of these strains were sequenced using the Illumina Mi-Seq technology.

description.title: Microbe sample from Xylella fastidiosa
description.comment: Xylella fastidiosa is a xylem-limited phytopathogenic bacterium endemic to the Americas, but that recently emerged in Asia and Europe. Albeit it is a quarantine organism for the European Union, importation of plant material from contaminated areas and latent infection in asymptomatic plants rendered its introduction inevitable. In 2012, four coffee plants (Coffea arabica and C. canephora) with leaf scorch symptoms growing in a confined glasshouse were detected in France. After identification of the causal agent, this outbreak was eradicated. Three X. fastidiosa strains were isolated from these plants confirming a preliminary diagnostic based on immunofluorescence. The strains were characterized by multiplex PCR and by multilocus sequence analysis / typing (MLSA-MLST) based on seven housekeeping genes. One strain, CFBP 8073, which was isolated from C. canephora imported from Mexico was assigned to X. fastidiosa subsp. fastidiosa/sandyi and presented a novel sequence type (ST) with novel alleles at two loci. The two other strains, CFBP 8072 and 8074, isolated from C. arabica imported from Ecuador were allocated to X. fastidiosa subsp. pauca. These two strains presented an identical novel ST with novel alleles at two loci. These MLST profiles evidenced recombination events. We provided genome sequences for CFBP 8072 and 8073 strains. Comparative analyses of the two new X. fastidiosa genome sequences with publicly available data, including the Italian strain CoDiRO, confirmed these phylogenetic positions and provided candidate alleles for coffee adaptation. This study confirms the global diversity of X. fastidiosa and highlights the diversity of strains isolated from coffee.

description.title: Microbe sample from Xylella fastidiosa subsp. multiplex
description.comment: Xylella fastidiosa, a bacterial plant pathogen confined in the past to the Americas, recently emerged in Europe. It was first reported in natural settings in France from Polygala myrtifolia shrubs in Corsica in July 2015 and in south-eastern mainland France in October 2015. These ornamentals were symptomatic and presented severe leaf scorches. All contaminated samples from France presented bacteria belonging to X. fastidiosa subsp. multiplex, based on multiprimer PCR (Hernandez-Martinez et al., Phytopathol. 2006) analyses run on DNAs extracted from the infected plant samples. A MLST scheme was used to type these bacteria which are characterized by two X. fastidiosa subsp. multiplex bona fide sequence types, ST6 and ST7. Three strains were isolated from Polygala myrtifolia (CFBP 8416; ST7) and Spartium junceum (CFBP 8417 and CFBP 8418; ST6). The genomes of these strains were sequenced using the Illumina Mi-Seq technology.

description.title: Microbe sample from Xylella fastidiosa subsp. fastidiosa CFBP7969
description.comment: Xylella fastidiosa is a bacterial plant pathogen disseminated across the Americas, while its presence is currently described in several European countries. Seven strains, available at the CIRM-CFBP (http://www.angers-nantes.inra.fr/cfbp/) were selected. Six strains were isolated in the USA from Vitis rotundifolia (CFBP7969), Vitis vinifera (CFBP 7970), Vitis SP (CFBP8341), Prunus dulcis (CFBP 8071) and Ambrosia artemifolia (CFBP 8082) and belong to X. fastidiosa subsp. fastidiosa. One strain was isolated in the USA from Vinca sp. (CFBP 8078) and belongs to X. fastidiosa subsp. multiplex. One strain was isolated from a coffee plant imported from the Costa Rica and intercepted in France (CFBP 8356) and belongs to X. fastidiosa subsp. sandyi. The taxonomic assignation to a subpecies was based on multiprimer PCR (Hernandez-Martinez et al., 2006), MLST scheme using 7 housekeeping genes (Yuan et al., 2010) and whole-genome sequencing unsing the Illumina Mi-Seq technology.

description.title: Microbe sample from Xylella fastidiosa subsp. multiplex CFBP8078
description.comment: Xylella fastidiosa is a bacterial plant pathogen disseminated across the Americas, while its presence is currently described in several European countries. Seven strains, available at the CIRM-CFBP (http://www.angers-nantes.inra.fr/cfbp/) were selected. Six strains were isolated in the USA from Vitis rotundifolia (CFBP7969), Vitis vinifera (CFBP 7970), Vitis SP (CFBP8341), Prunus dulcis (CFBP 8071) and Ambrosia artemifolia (CFBP 8082) and belong to X. fastidiosa subsp. fastidiosa. One strain was isolated in the USA from Vinca sp. (CFBP 8078) and belongs to X. fastidiosa subsp. multiplex. One strain was isolated from a coffee plant imported from the Costa Rica and intercepted in France (CFBP 8356) and belongs to X. fastidiosa subsp. sandyi. The taxonomic assignation to a subpecies was based on multiprimer PCR (Hernandez-Martinez et al., 2006), MLST scheme using 7 housekeeping genes (Yuan et al., 2010) and whole-genome sequencing unsing the Illumina Mi-Seq technology.

bioprojects.title: Xylella fastidiosa subsp. pauca strain:CFBP8072 Genome sequencing and assembly

description.title: Microbe sample from Xylella fastidiosa subsp. pauca
description.comment: Xylella fastidiosa is a xylem-limited phytopathogenic bacterium endemic to the Americas, but that recently emerged in Asia and Europe. Albeit it is a quarantine organism for the European Union, importation of plant material from contaminated areas and latent infection in asymptomatic plants rendered its introduction inevitable. In 2012, four coffee plants (Coffea arabica and C. canephora) with leaf scorch symptoms growing in a confined glasshouse were detected in France. After identification of the causal agent, this outbreak was eradicated. Three X. fastidiosa strains were isolated from these plants confirming a preliminary diagnostic based on immunofluorescence. The strains were characterized by multiplex PCR and by multilocus sequence analysis / typing (MLSA-MLST) based on seven housekeeping genes. One strain, CFBP 8073, which was isolated from C. canephora imported from Mexico was assigned to X. fastidiosa subsp. fastidiosa/sandyi and presented a novel sequence type (ST) with novel alleles at two loci. The two other strains, CFBP 8072 and 8074, isolated from C. arabica imported from Ecuador were allocated to X. fastidiosa subsp. pauca. These two strains presented an identical novel ST with novel alleles at two loci. These MLST profiles evidenced recombination events. We provided genome sequences for CFBP 8072 and 8073 strains. Comparative analyses of the two new X. fastidiosa genome sequences with publicly available data, including the Italian strain CoDiRO, confirmed these phylogenetic positions and provided candidate alleles for coffee adaptation. This study confirms the global diversity of X. fastidiosa and highlights the diversity of strains isolated from coffee.
